tasks.label: Console  →  isthislegit Server window + http://127.0.0.1:4000
tasks.detail: Opens the operator console app. Starts everything and administers it: server, LiveKit, Caddy, database, migrations, seed, invite codes, accounts, storage, retention, updates, configuration. Closing the window hides it to the tray; Quit from the tray stops the services it started.

tasks.label: Desktop app (dev)
tasks.detail: electron-vite dev. Opens the Electron client; it talks to http://localhost:3000 unless you change the server address on the sign-in screen.

tasks.label: Android app (dev)
tasks.detail: expo start. Prints a QR code; scan it with Expo Go on the phone and the app runs there with live reload -- no Android SDK, no Gradle, nothing to install on this machine. Point it at a server on the sign-in screen, using this machine's LAN address rather than localhost, which on a phone is the phone.

tasks.label: Compile server
tasks.detail: tsc for packages/shared, then nest build for apps/server. The fast inner loop, and what catches a type error. The console's Build button runs the same thing and can Restart afterwards, which this cannot.

tasks.label: Typecheck client
tasks.detail: tsc --noEmit over apps/desktop. Its own task because electron-vite strips types with esbuild and never checks them -- a client build alone will happily package code that does not compile. Both client packaging runs depend on this.

tasks.label: Typecheck Android client
tasks.detail: tsc --noEmit over mobile. Its own task for the reason the desktop one is: Metro strips types with Babel and never checks them, so a bundle will happily ship code that does not compile. The packaging task depends on this.

tasks.label: Set version
tasks.detail: Asks for a version, then writes it to every package.json in the workspace and to package-lock.json. Do this before packaging a client: publishing refuses a version that is not newer than the one already published, and the version in apps/desktop/package.json is what electron-builder stamps into latest.yml and what an installed client compares itself against.

tasks.label: Build and package server  →  release\isthislegit-server-<v>-setup.exe
tasks.detail: infra\installer\build-server-installer.ps1. Builds shared, the server and the admin app, stages them with pinned dependency versions, and wraps the lot as the installer you copy to the server machine. Several minutes: it runs a production npm install into the staging tree and packages Electron. Run the installer there as administrator, or it skips the database setup and the boot tasks.

tasks.label: Build and package client  →  apps\desktop\release\isthislegit-<v>-setup.exe
tasks.detail: Typecheck, then electron-builder. Produces the installer, its .blockmap and latest.yml -- the three files an update is made of, and the same build that publishing sends to the server. Run Set version first: publishing refuses a version that is not newer than the one already published, and an installed client only offers an update if the published version is higher than its own. Then infra\publish-desktop-update.ps1 uploads it; the server box cannot build this itself.

tasks.label: Set Android version
tasks.detail: Asks for a version and writes it to mobile\package.json, which app.config.js reads for both the version people see and the Android versionCode derived from it. A separate task because mobile sits outside the root workspaces glob on purpose, so the workspace-wide Set version deliberately does not reach it. Do this before packaging: publishing refuses a versionCode that has not risen, and Android refuses to install one that has not either.

tasks.label: Build and package Android client  →  mobile\release\isthislegit-<v>.apk
tasks.detail: Typecheck, then scripts\build-apk.mjs: generates mobile\android if needed, runs gradlew assembleRelease, verifies the APK is not debug-signed, and writes the APK plus the latest.json that publishes it. Needs the Android SDK and JDK 17 -- see mobile\README.md, which also covers the release keystore. That keystore is the one setup step here that cannot be undone: sign a later build with a different key and every phone refuses the update. Run Set Android version first. Then infra\publish-android-update.ps1 uploads it.

tasks.label: Rebuild Android project  →  mobile\android
tasks.detail: expo prebuild --clean. Throws mobile\android away and regenerates it from app.json, app.config.js and plugins\. Needed after changing any of those three, and the thing to try when a Gradle build fails for a reason that makes no sense. The directory is generated and not committed, so nothing is lost. The packaging task creates it on its own the first time; this is only for replacing one.

tasks.label: Install Android client on a plugged-in phone
tasks.detail: adb install -r on whatever mobile\release holds. For putting a build on your own phone without publishing it to everyone -- the phone needs developer options and USB debugging on, and adb comes from the SDK's platform-tools. -r reinstalls over an existing copy and keeps its data, which only works while the signing key stays the same.
tasks.command: $apk = Get-ChildItem mobile\release\*.apk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1; if (-not $apk) { Write-Host '  x No APK in mobile\release. Run the packaging task first.' -ForegroundColor Red; exit 1 }; Write-Host "  Installing $($apk.Name)..."; adb install -r $apk.FullName

inputs.description: New version for every package in the workspace, e.g. 0.2.3
New version for the Android client, e.g. 0.2.3 (minor and patch stay under 100)
